# Goverdhan Gajjala — FIRST-HAND rules from the Northern Virginia IBD Meetup webinar

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CI7mNvEQyms ("Goverdhan Gajjala - Trading Webinar"), ~1 h 50 min,
recorded late Feb 2024 (he shows trades from "February 8 2024, a couple of weeks ago"). Transcript pasted by Ajay
2026-10-13; timestamps are the transcript's. Everything below is GG speaking (first_hand = true). Quotes are
verbatim from the auto-caption (grammar as spoken); [brackets] are my clarifications.

## Identity of the method
- 9:45 "I consider myself as a intraday swing trader … a mix of Minervini style swing trading in intraday … I'm not
  compromising on the magnitude of the moves, there will be better magnitude in less duration moves."
- 10:19 "I only do long side trading, I don't short."
- 12:00 "I'm a 100% technical trader … I don't look at the news much … I just trade the price and volume action."
- 11:37 "I developed five to six go-to chart setups."

## SCANNER (the only numbers he gives anywhere)
- 19:12–19:51 "the watch list scanner that I developed … the price of the stock anything from **50 cents to $100** …
  volume should be **minimum 1 million** volume and then percentage change from the previous day **at least minimum 25%**
  change … then it comes to my small caps watch list."
- 1:32:02 Q "minimum volume you look for in a small cap" → "the minimum is **1 million** volume in my scanner … the more the better."
- 19:59 also watches the **Zendoo** YouTube live momentum scanner all day (secondary source of names).
- 1:21:56 premarket stock selection: "ThinkorSwim has this **pre-market movers** scanner … I **sort by volume** … and
  also I look at the **percentage gainers** [ToS built-in] … as soon as the market opens this gets filled … I sort by the
  percentage change, see which are the biggest movers."
- 1:23:30 how much premarket volume: "the bigger the volume the better … 1 million volume and the price is only $2 and
  it's just one bar in five minutes and after that it was fading out — I'm not interested at all. Now the volume is
  picking up, 2.6 million, 3 million … the volume is sustaining and it's increasing … this gradual increase in volume
  catches my attention."
- 1:15:24 float: "if it's a low float stock and the float is rotating millions of times, each five minute bar has 4
  million 5 million … volume is a must to me … I combine that with the float information … when the float is low when
  there is volume there can be halt-up kind of magnitude move."
- 1:44:09 float source: ToS "shares" column (= float). 1:26:55 "BS … shares column this is only 624,000, this is ultra
  low float … volume 60 million today."
- 21:04 "the reversal squeeze happens only in the low float stocks, the lower the float the better."
- No numeric float threshold is ever stated. No short-interest number is ever stated.

## TIMEFRAMES / INDICATORS
- 1:40:07 "I tried 1 minute 3 minute 5 minute 15 minutes … I concluded on the **five minute** … 5 minute is my favorite."
- 1:21:40 "I usually switch between **five and 15 minutes**."
- 25:36 "this is the **9 EMA**, this is the **21 EMA**." (both on every chart; the TraderLion screenshot shows
  MovAvgExponential(CLOSE,9) and (CLOSE,21) on a 5m chart with premarket shown and a VolumeAvg line under volume.)
- 1:19:00 daily context: "even though this is a 5 minute chart I always go and look at the daily … draw the support and
  resistance … I zoom out." 1:46:33 "I align my intraday thesis with the daily … continuation run … more confidence."
- 46:21 "I don't look at the level two." 45:50 no leverage in small caps.

## DAILY ROUTINE
- Premarket 13:21–14:34: "in the pre-market I'll see what's moving, I'll open my scanner … ToS pre-market mover scanner
  and the Zendoo online scanner … if it's making some noise in pre-market I put them in my watch list and also there
  will be some stocks which make **after hours moves from the past day, I'll keep them as well** … focus list one,
  two, three … if there is no action I'll go meditate … towards the market open I'll be ready."
- 14:41 "**I don't take trades for the first 15 minutes after the market opens** … I want to see the direction … whenever
  I tried trading right at the open most of the times I ended up in losses."
- 1:26:03 "at a time I'll be watching closely **four or five stocks** … up to 18 on three screens."
- 1:26:48 last two hours: "yes … towards the market close sometimes this will squeeze up … and squeeze up after hours
  too, that's why I'll actively watch it towards the close."
- 1:16:35 pre/after-hours execution: "**limit orders only** … slippage … I trade with **less size** after and pre-market."
- 15:17 whole-day presence when the market is good; 15:32 "if most stocks are in downtrend, the volume is low like in
  summers, I don't look at the screens, I take the day off."
- 49:48 trades per day: "if the market is good on average **two, three, four trades per day**"; zero on quiet days.

## POST-MARKET / WEEKLY ROUTINE
- 15:57–17:03 journal by hand during the day: "I took this trade, I grade the setup **A+ or B**, why I'm taking a B,
  my patience level, was I patient enough or an impulse trade, my discipline … how I peeled off"; at end of day
  "**screenshots of each of the trades** into Google Slides."
- 17:03–18:16 weekend: video-record the impactful trades **and the missed trades** with ToS OnDemand, Camtasia
  fast-forward, review in <10 minutes; TraderSync for stats.

## SITUATIONAL AWARENESS (market-condition read for his strategy)
- 43:39–44:37 "in a good day there will be a couple of **100%+ runners** … as soon as the market opens I see three, four:
  one 400% runner, one 300% runner because they ran after hours or pre-market … then a bunch of **90+ / 80+** runners.
  On a very bad day the maximum runners would be **30%–40%** and two, three, four of them, and then others 10%, 20% —
  that tells me the market is not strong for my strategy, it's quiet."
- 45:24 honours it: trades "very less" in quiet weeks.

## THE FIVE SETUPS (all 5-min, all long, all "stop = low of the previous bar / base")
Common 34:45: "all these setups have the same criteria: good demand, very shallow pullback with low volume, very
constructive action, and if it takes the previous highs — enter; stop loss would be the low of the base."

### 1. Bull Flag (fastest) 21:45–24:37
- "gradual increase in price along with gradual increase in volume [2–3 green bars], then almost sideways or very
  shallow pullback with less volume compared to the left side."
- Entry: "taking the highs of that previous green bar"; Stop: "the low of that bar."
- "the pullback is one bar, usually two to three bars … it happens within 10 minutes and takes off, this is the fastest."
- 23:02 can form in premarket ("pre-market action with good volume … constructive shallow pullback … as soon as the
  market opens it squeezes").

### 2. EMA Kiss and Fly 31:33–32:41
- "extension of bull flag where the left side won't be that strong, only two green bars or one green bar … it waits
  more and **honors the 9 EMA** whenever it pulls back … within the pullback the volume will be considerably low
  compared to the green bars … touches the EMA, honors it — that would be my entry [high of the bar that kissed the EMA]
  and the exit [stop] below the low of the previous bar."

### 3. Horizontal Fade 32:49–33:50, 1:20:08–1:21:47
- "longer extension of both setups: left side strong, gradually goes sideways with low volume pullback towards the
  high of the price action, shallow very clean pullback, and when the **9 EMA and 21 EMA merge** around that area then
  slowly the momentum starts … risk very tiny below the previous bar." "If I flip to 15 minutes it looks even better."
- 1:20:08 "not something that happens very often."

### 4. Intraday VCP (slowest) 33:50–34:37
- "left side good demand, then it **honors the 21 EMA** when it pulls back with less volume … in each cycle it honors the
  21 EMA and the volatility contracts in each cycle … the entry would be the top of this [last] cycle and the stop loss
  the low of this cycle … it should have this uptrend look."

### 5. Reversal Squeeze 35:02–35:56 (+ 36:12–38:18 example, 1:04:36)
- "happens only mostly in low float stocks, the lower the float the better … **tennis ball action**: whenever there is a
  drop it tries to squeeze up, whenever it hits the ground it bounces back hard … when the volume picks up it squeezes,
  explosive moves … whenever it tries to sell off it [re]takes the previous highs … at the morning open it tried to sell
  off completely and then bumps up and waits and then makes explosive move."
- 36:12 example: premarket news, low float, grinding up at the top of the range; volume picked up ~7:30 CT and again
  into the open; at the open tried the premarket highs, failed (sell-off, "tennis ball"), dropped big, squeezed back,
  halted; then "the pullback is very gradual, all at the top of this bar with gradual decrease in volume … as soon as
  the selling pressure is reduced and the demand kicks in, explosive." Entry = when it takes the highs after that quiet
  pullback (same entry rule); made the move into the close and after hours.
- 59:24 "most of the stocks make a big move after hours"; 1:26:55 watches the close for it.

## ENTRY MECHANICS
- 1:40:56–1:41:55 "when it's breaking out I anticipate the volume is going to follow … I just look at the price …
  **I'll enter right at the break** [of the previous bar's high]; sometimes I wait for the bar to close and enter in the
  next bar."
- 32:27 "most of my exits [stops] are below the low of the previous bar, always; tight risk-reward entries always."
- 1:17:12 shakeout: "if it stops me out I won't re-enter right then … I need at least a couple of bars to see whether the
  action is good."
- 56:27 goes "all in" only on an A+ setup with a profit cushion; otherwise half size then add.

## TRADE MANAGEMENT
- 24:46–26:40 "if it doesn't go in my direction I exit right below this bar. If it goes … I want to be patient … give it
  **15 minutes, three bars** … then peel off **1/3 or half** … trail the remaining along the **9 EMA** (mix with the 21)
  … or 1/3, 1/3, 1/3."
- 39:03 "once the price goes in my direction I **move my stop loss to break even** … then I added half, double the size
  with zero risk."
- 40:54–41:18 **base counting**: "first base, second base, third base, this is a climax run … I was peeling off early."
  1:00:37 "fourth base, I came out of everything."
- 48:29 if volume dries while in profit: "take some partial off … remaining at the buy point … chip up."
- 1:42:51 stops: "most of the times hard stops, sometimes mental stops when I'm watching with size … when I step away
  I put a hard stop."
- 1:12:47 "hold period on average for a winning trade is 45 minutes to 1 hour; for a losing trade 10 minutes."

## RISK / SIZING
- 26:47–28:01 progressive exposure (Minervini): winning → bigger size, drawdown → smaller; A+ setup → double size.
- 46:47–48:12 "if $2,000 is the loss in one trade, next trade I cut to $1,000 … then $500"; after wins scale up
  (2k → 3k–4k risk). No hard daily max loss, but losses reduce size.
- 1:47:23 risk per trade: "I do it very fast like **5% to 10%**, then 2.5%, 2% … beginners 1% or 0.25% … in drawdowns
  1%." (Research 2026-10-13: 0.25% was HIS OWN starting risk per trade — masterclass + his X post 2024-01-30 — not only a
  beginner figure; the basis of the 5–10% is ambiguous in the talk.) 1:44:56 first year "$20 risk per trade".
- 1:48:40 average R:R "3.5, 4 to 1".
- 1:12:00 2023 stats: 745 closing trades, win 31% / loss 68%; profitable second half: 165 trades, same ~30/70 win rate
  with larger average winners.

## WHAT HE AVOIDS / INVALIDATIONS (1:04:13–1:11:07)
- Entering on bias from the premarket run without a formed setup; re-entering bigger after a stop (revenge).
- "left side not strong … climax bar then reversal … green bar with big volume but bad close and short range = selling."
- Dangerous: a base forming inside a big-volume selling bar — wait for it to reclaim the highs and build another tight base.
- Never 1-minute charts; never shorts; no overnight holds in low floats.

# PART 2 — FIRST-HAND rules from the TraderLion podcast (Jan 2024) — timestamps below are THIS video (S9), not the webinar

Source: https://youtu.be/10pHBNVi4Jc "+805% Trading Champion of 2023 Reveals His Powerful Day Trading Setups"
(Richard Moglen interviews GG, ~2 h 19 min). Transcript pasted by Ajay 2026-10-13. GG speaking unless noted.

## Scanner / universe (confirms the webinar numbers)
- 22:10 "I created my own scanner, small cap volatility scanner … any stock which is **above 50 cents and max $100**
  and the **volume should be 1 million** and **at least up by 25%**, show me all these stocks."
- 22:42 Zendoo live scanner on YouTube all day as the second feed; "in two years I covered all the top movers within that range."
- 24:07 "I prefer more liquid stocks … volume is a must … I don't take the trades which have less volume even though
  the price move is big."
- 25:42 "around 12 to 15 stocks [on the list], out of them maybe four, two stocks will be moving on average … four to
  five active stocks."
- 1:36:58 PXMD: "bull flag but low volume, like 200k … whenever there is this kind of not-so-good volume I take the
  appropriate size, not the full size."

## Chart
- 24:42 "I'll have a **9 EMA and 21 EMA**, I have this price and then this volume, that's all. My chart has nothing
  else, I don't have VWAP or ADRs. I'm strictly price and volume based."
- 21:51 "mainly the **five minute and 15 minute** charts." 1:13:06 tried 1/3/10-min; 5 and 15 are "cleaner, less noise".

## Daily-chart short-squeeze read (the "squeeze potential" chapter)
- 52:49–53:46 LIFW daily: "it has a **history of prior runs, history of squeezes** … it tried to go up, got faded out,
  then it takes all these highs again on the daily, higher again, tries to fade out, takes the highs out — these are
  all features of short squeezing — then it completely fades out, shows strength again and squeezes all the way up.
  When **the daily and the intraday have the congruence**, the move is going to be exponential … the probability is
  always high."
- 1:01:02 POLA: "you see the similar patterns in the daily too: demand shows up, tries to fade out, but the squeeze
  will be much bigger … the shorts have to cover and they turn as buyers."
- 1:11:08 a stock that ran 1,000%+ two days ago: "has a strong feature of short squeezing" — stays on the radar.
- 1:17:32 "once a stock makes a move it will stay a couple of days, make noise a couple of days, then completely fades
  out … when the volume dries up and the price is falling slowly I move it to the third monitor, the **graveyard
  watch list**."
- 2:02:47 "next-day multi-day movers: previous-day strength, after hours a big move, next day if it tries to form a
  setup I enter — a continuation."

## Reversal Squeeze — his own slide text (2:01:46–2:02:40)
- "squeeze up reversal: **the lower the float the better; good volume; already strong demand, especially when the
  price goes down it almost immediately comes up like a ball under the water**; it usually gets dumped but rises
  quickly back and waits; it has tried to squeeze up in the past bars — look of going up but sold off; this time the
  sell-off was big and the bounce back was quick." Q: undercut of the base ok? "yes, it has that look of a ball
  bouncing back." "when it squeezes, all the short sellers have to convert to buyers."
- 2:00:32 **halts playbook**: "history of halts, good green volume popping up, price should go up … a halt is nothing
  but too much demand in a very short time … low float — even lesser volume will make too much of an up move and halt
  the stock. That characteristic is what makes the short squeeze setups. There will be up squeezes but no down squeezes."
- 55:18–57:49 halts: "halting up — I feel it has a higher chance of going up … in low floats when it halts up it
  continues the momentum … once a stock is this strong, 100% in 20 minutes, it tends to move sideways; **if it moves
  sideways with less volume and forms another base, high chance it has an even bigger move**."

## The other setups — his slide text (1:54:46–1:59:51)
- Common 1:54:53 "strong demand, goes sideways at the top of the bars, volume subsides in those bars, and if it
  reclaims the highs — this is the concept of all the moves."
- EMA kiss and fly 1:55:28: "it will honor the EMAs — the **9 EMA touch and go**, touch and go, ride it higher …
  1 demand is good, 2 price pulls back organically, 3 volume reduces in the pullback, 4 price touches and respects the EMA."
- Strong demand slow fader (= horizontal fade) 1:56:08: "this is like a **bull flag in the 15 minute chart** … goes
  sideways at the very high of the price, volume subsiding, then if it picks up I take the call." 2:00:12 "price goes
  sideways at the top of the highs, selling gradually [dries], consolidates at the EMAs, the look of wanting to go higher."
- Bull flag 1:59:24: "**at least two big green bars** (three is good) with a good price increase; the next few bars
  consolidate around the top with low-volume bars; **entry at the top of the pullback bar, exit [stop] at the bottom of it**."
  58:27 ICCT: reclaiming the highs within 2 bars = "I'm strong enough, I don't want to wait for a normal consolidation."
- 1:59:01 combined setups: "if a setup has two or three setups mixed together — a reversal setup on the daily and a
  bull flag intraday — the certainty of the move is higher."
- 1:57:33 the lowest-volume bar right before the move (said about the strong-demand SLOW FADER = Horizontal Fade, "like
  a vcp characteristics too"): "volume completely dried out and the price is not going down … then it makes a big move."

## Entry / orders
- 1:03:33 "I have like one hour to take the call … I don't want to be the first one in; I want the price and volume
  to prove it."
- 54:24 two nearby highs (4.59 vs 4.65): "I want to be more careful and have this [higher] high as my buy point."
- 1:00:05 "I **market order** everything … I'm okay with the slippage … even stop-loss orders, I want to be executed."
  (Webinar: limit orders only outside regular hours.)
- 35:24 "I don't put any stop loss in the software, it's a mental stop … as soon as it triggers my buy point and goes
  in my direction, **my buy price is the stop loss**."

## Sizing / risk / stats
- 33:31–34:28 medium size "10, 20%" of the account when in drawdown; all in on the clean A+ setup with a profit cushion.
- 44:06 drawdown rule: "if I'm in a **−10% or −15% drawdown**: next five trades should be only **−5% together** …
  reduce the size, get some wins, build confidence, then slowly go big."
- 37:47–39:14 TraderSync 2023: 745 trades, win 31% / loss 68%, avg loser −4.06%, avg winner +8.55%; last six months
  165 trades, win 28%, avg loser −4%, avg winner +13% (~4:1); 17 consecutive losses in June; 511 losers in the year.
- 1:28:10 "last six months I take one trade per day, two trades maximum." 1:29:16 A+ setups "one or two every week."
- 13:49 "I went big when there was a clear setup, easy trade … all in in those setups."

## Exits
- 49:49 "always sell into strength … 1/3, half … 1/3 1/3 1/3 … not optimal; this year I want to scale IN: peel 1/3 if
  strong and add that 1/3 back, so I have gains even if it reverses."
- 1:09:11 exhaustion: "when the intraday action is that big it won't run that big in after hours … and the
  **psychological levels of $5, $10** get into the picture" — sold TPST into $10. 1:21:19 "$1 psychological level,
  when it takes 1.04 I'm interested." 1:39:13 "it's going to stop at five … climax run, took it at 4.7."

## Post-market / premarket
- 1:16:13 "these stocks run big in the post market; **in the post market the run will be much smoother, the volume
  will be low, but the magnitude of the squeezes will be huge** compared to market hours … when it has this kind of
  action in market hours and starts to go up during the market end it goes very big … I started trading after hours
  too, and I do very less pre-market trading."
- 1:14:05 AVGR: squeezed $7→$12 in one 5-min bar after hours; next day watched for the reversal/squeeze feature;
  the big move came after hours again.

## Mistakes he names (for the "what not to do" panel)
- Forcing entries from premarket bias; re-entering bigger after a stop; trading after a huge after-hours run assuming
  a repeat; entering a half-position on a "feel" without a setup; selling on P&L instead of on price action.
